title: Start from random weights, no imitation
text: rl-v2 tests whether the GA genome is a head start or a ceiling: same network, inputs and PPO as rl-v1, only the start changes. Self-play first, then the bots, then every earlier model.
rejected: Imitation first (that is rl-v1); a new architecture (would mix two changes into one comparison).

title: Stage 1 ends on a plateau, not a score
text: The first start ended self-play after 12 iterations, when it beat the bots 50% of the time. Self-play is the point of the project, so stage 1 now runs until the score against the GA genome has not improved for 60 iterations (at most 400): it shows how far self-play gets alone.
rejected: A fixed bots threshold (ended the stage after 3 minutes); a fixed iteration count (could stop while it is still learning, or waste hours on a plateau).

title: 1,500 games per iteration
text: Random players make long games with ~210 decisions each; 3,000 of them (rl-v1's setting) ran the 8 GB laptop out of memory. 1,500 fit with room for the evaluation.
rejected: Keeping 3,000 with float16 features (a change to the shared code that rl-v1 does not have).

title: Same evaluation games as rl-v1
text: The per-iteration evaluation and the goal checks use rl-v1's and az-v1's seeds, so every number compares directly with them. A new confirmation seed is kept for the end.

title: Checked: +Actions, +Cards and +Buys work
text: New tests (tests/test_vanilla.py): every card's +Cards/+Actions/+Buys/+$ is right in the engine, and in C-engine games through the network's decision interface a player is asked again after a Village or a Market, never beyond what the bonuses allow. The trained net uses a second buy as often as the GA genome (76% vs 72% of the turns it played a +Buy card), but it rarely chains actions: 0.51 actions per turn and 6% of turns with 2+ actions, against rl-v1's 1.61 and 28%. Self-play from zero found money + attacks (Witch, Militia, Gardens) and not engines (experiments/turn_usage.py).
